question: What is the maximum number of words permitted on every static regulatory or warning sign?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not contain any provision establishing a maximum number of words for static regulatory or warning signs. The only message-length limits in the evidence apply to changeable message signs (limits on phases and lines of text, not word counts), so this question cannot be answered from the available material. Standards (mandatory): - The closest related provision addresses changeable message signs, not static signs: "Each message shall consist of no more than two phases. A phase shall consist of no more than three lines of text." This limits phases and lines on CMS displays and does not set a word maximum for static regulatory or warning signs. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-1 shows conspicuity enhancements (plaques, flags, beacons, LEDs) but no word-count limit; [Image 2] Figure 6G-1 shows temporary traffic control regulatory signs of varying word lengths (e.g., "STAY IN LANE TO MERGE POINT") with no stated word maximum; [Image 3] Table 2B-1 addresses minimum sign sizes, not word counts; [Image 4] Table 6G-1 addresses sign sizes for TTC zones, not word counts; [Images 5–8] show sign size applicability text, roundabout signing examples, and intersection approach sign placement, none of which specify a maximum word count. Citations: - Section 2L.05 Standard §4 (p.515) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Figure 6G-1 (p.794) - Table 2B-1 (p.67) - Table 6G-1 (p.793)
